backlog.alm.defaultSolutionComponents.gi: {count} custom components whose only solution membership is the default solution
backlog.alm.defaultSolutionComponents.te: Export and import into a clean environment and use the application. The components that get missed are the ones nothing visibly depends on until somebody runs the process that needs them.
backlog.alm.defaultSolutionComponents.th: An export of the named solutions carries every one of them, and an import into a clean environment produces a working application
backlog.alm.defaultSolutionComponents.wh: Each has been added to a named solution with a meaningful publisher prefix
backlog.alm.environmentVariableWithDefau: The environment variable {componentName}, shipping a default value
Import into a clean environment and confirm the dependent component fails or warns rather than silently using the development value.
An import into an environment where the pipeline has not set it leaves the variable visibly empty
The default has been removed and the value is set per environment by the pipeline
backlog.alm.hardCodedEnvironmentValue.te: Import into a second environment with the variable unset and confirm it fails visibly rather than running against the wrong target. A default value shipped with the definition reproduces the original problem with more steps.
backlog.alm.hardCodedEnvironmentValue.th: The component resolves the value per environment, and an import into an environment where it is unset surfaces it as missing
backlog.alm.hardCodedEnvironmentValue.wh: The value comes from an environment variable with no default
backlog.alm.missingConnectionReference.g: The flow {componentName}, carrying a connection rather than a connection reference
backlog.alm.missingConnectionReference.t: Import into an environment that has never held this solution and run the flow. Testing in an environment where the connection already exists proves nothing, because it resolves by accident.
The solution imports into a second environment and the flow runs there after the reference is bound, with no edit to the flow itself
backlog.alm.missingConnectionReference.w: A connection reference exists per connector and the flow points at it
backlog.alm.publisherPrefixSprawl.testRe: None on the existing components. Renaming a prefix is not something the platform permits, and attempting it is how a solution gets broken by a finding whose severity is low.
backlog.alm.publisherPrefixSprawl.then: Components created after that date use the agreed prefix
backlog.alm.publisherPrefixSprawl.when: A prefix has been agreed for new work and written where a new developer will find it
backlog.alm.unmanagedInProduction.given: Unmanaged customisations in the production environment {evidenceValue}
backlog.alm.unmanagedInProduction.testRe: Make a change in development, promote it, and confirm it arrives in production without anybody opening a maker portal there. Also confirm a change made directly in production is visible as an unmanaged layer, because that is how the next one gets caught.
backlog.alm.unmanagedInProduction.then: No new unmanaged customisation appears in production, and what is there has been captured into a solution that can be exported
backlog.alm.unmanagedInProduction.when: A development environment is the source of truth and a pipeline promotes managed solutions into production
backlog.architecture.externalLogicInvisi: Confirm the recorded owner acknowledges it. An owner written down without being told is a name, not an owner.
The architecture documentation names the service, its owner, its repository and what happens when it is unavailable
An owner and a repository have been recorded for what sits behind it
backlog.architecture.logicSpread.given: The table {tableName}, with logic in {count} different places
backlog.architecture.logicSpread.testReq: Create, update and delete a record and confirm every expected side effect happens, in the expected order, once. The failure this rule exists for is a side effect happening twice, or not at all, depending on which mechanism ran first.
backlog.architecture.logicSpread.then: The map exists as a document a new developer can read, and the number of distinct mechanisms firing on that table has gone down
backlog.architecture.logicSpread.when: The execution order on create and on update has been mapped and the consolidation agreed in that map has been done
backlog.architecture.proCodeWhereConfigW: The form script {componentName}, doing only visibility and validation
Walk every branch of the original script on the form. Business rules evaluate differently from an onload handler, particularly on a record that opens with the condition already met.
The same fields show, hide, enable and require under the same conditions, and the script is no longer registered on the form
It has been replaced with a business rule
backlog.featureNotStory: Created as a feature rather than a story.
backlog.featureNotStoryDetail: It was sized at 21 points, which means it needs splitting before it goes in a sprint.
backlog.governance.orphanedByOwner.given: The {componentType} {componentName}, owned by a disabled or absent user
backlog.governance.orphanedByOwner.testR: Confirm the connections it uses were also reassigned. Changing the owner without changing the connections leaves it running on the departed person's authentication until that expires.
backlog.governance.orphanedByOwner.then: The component runs on credentials that do not belong to one person, and its run history continues uninterrupted
backlog.governance.orphanedByOwner.when: Ownership has moved to a service principal or a solution owned by a group
backlog.governance.orphanedColumn.given: {count} custom columns on {tableName} with no form, view, flow or plugin reference
backlog.governance.orphanedColumn.testRe: Check the audit history or API usage for writes to each column over a full business cycle before deleting any of them. This rule cannot see an integration, and its finding is a question rather than an instruction.
backlog.governance.orphanedColumn.then: Columns confirmed unused are deleted, and columns written by an integration are documented as such rather than deleted
backlog.governance.orphanedColumn.when: Each has been checked for integration traffic and a decision recorded
backlog.governance.securityRoleSprawl.gi: The security role {componentName}, assigned to no user and no team
backlog.governance.securityRoleSprawl.te: Check whether a provisioning process assigns it on a schedule before deleting. A role assigned monthly by an automated job looks unassigned for twenty-nine days out of thirty.
backlog.governance.securityRoleSprawl.th: The role no longer appears in the role picker
backlog.governance.securityRoleSprawl.wh: It has been confirmed that nothing assigns it and it has been deleted
backlog.layer.band: The band default for this rule. This finding was not estimated individually.
backlog.layer.model: Produced by a model, one finding at a time.
backlog.layer.override: Set by a consultant on this engagement.
backlog.lifecycle.classicWorkflowDormant: The classic workflow {componentName}, activated and with no execution recorded in ninety days
Create a record that matches its trigger conditions in a non production environment and watch whether it fires. That answers the question in ten minutes and no amount of reading the definition will.
Either it is deactivated and deleted, or a defect is raised saying why it should have run and did not
Somebody has established which of the two explanations applies
backlog.lifecycle.classicWorkflowInUse.t: Run both for an agreed period against the same data and compare the output before deactivating the original. A workflow replaced and deactivated in one deployment has no way back inside a change window.
The same records are produced, with the same values, for every trigger condition the workflow handled
backlog.lifecycle.classicWorkflowInUse.w: Its replacement is in place and the workflow is deactivated
backlog.lifecycle.customWorkflowActivity: The custom workflow activity {componentName}, called by at least one activated workflow

Exercise every calling workflow end to end against the new implementation. The activity's inputs and outputs are typed differently from a custom API's parameters, and a mapping error here produces a wrong value rather than an error.
No activated workflow references the activity, and the assembly can be removed without breaking an import
Its logic has been moved to a custom API or a plugin and every calling workflow has been repointed
backlog.lifecycle.dataflowPresent.testRe: Run both against the same source for one full cycle and compare row counts and a sample of values. Also confirm the Dataverse capacity consumption after the change, because that was half the reason for the finding.
backlog.lifecycle.dataflowPresent.then: The destination tables hold the same data after a full cycle, and the new implementation exists in source control
backlog.lifecycle.dataflowPresent.when: It has been rebuilt somewhere it can be versioned, or retired
backlog.lifecycle.deprecatedClientApi.gi: The web resource {componentName} calling a removed client API
backlog.lifecycle.deprecatedClientApi.te: Open each form the web resource is registered on and exercise the behaviour it controls. A removed API fails silently in some browsers and loudly in others, so a single browser check proves less than it appears to.
backlog.lifecycle.deprecatedClientApi.th: The Power Apps checker reports no deprecated client API findings for this web resource, and every form that loads it behaves as it did
backlog.lifecycle.deprecatedClientApi.wh: Each call has been replaced with its documented successor
backlog.lifecycle.dialogPresent.testRequ: Confirm nothing referenced it before deleting. A dialog is unreachable in the interface, so the only way it is still doing anything is through a link somebody built to it.
backlog.lifecycle.dialogPresent.then: No dialog records remain in the solution, and no security role, form or site map entry refers to one
backlog.lifecycle.rdlReport.testRequirem: Run the original and the replacement over the same period and reconcile the totals line by line. Reports disagree for reasons nobody predicts, usually a filter on a status nobody documented.
backlog.lifecycle.rdlReport.then: The decision names who uses the report and how often, and the replacement produces the same figures for an agreed reporting period
backlog.lifecycle.rdlReport.when: A decision has been recorded to delete it, rebuild it in Power BI, or replace it with a view
backlog.lowConfidenceDetail: Look at the component before planning with this number.
backlog.operability.noEnvironmentSeparat: The same solution present unmanaged in {count} environments with diverging versions

Before anything else, produce a written comparison of what differs between the environments. Picking a source without knowing what the others have that it does not is how a fortnight of somebody's undocumented work disappears.
A change made in the source environment reaches the others through a pipeline, and the divergence that existed has been reconciled and recorded
One environment has been made the source and the others receive managed solutions from it
backlog.operability.noFailureAlerting.gi: The analysed solutions, with no component reporting a failure to a person
backlog.operability.noFailureAlerting.te: Force a failure and confirm somebody receives it. Every other operability finding in this report assumes this one is done, so a notification that goes to an unmonitored mailbox invalidates the lot.
backlog.operability.noFailureAlerting.th: A failure in any monitored component produces a message naming the component, the time and the identifier needed to find the run
backlog.operability.noFailureAlerting.wh: A failure path exists that reaches an agreed channel
backlog.performance.plugSyncSlow.testReq: Measure the save time a user experiences, not the step duration in the trace. They are different numbers and the user only ever sees the first one.
backlog.performance.plugSyncSlow.then: The average execution time is below five hundred milliseconds, and the behaviour that moved still happens
backlog.performance.plugSyncSlow.when: Work that does not need to be in the transaction has moved out of it
backlog.performance.stepNoFilteringAttri: The update step {componentName}, registered with no filtering attributes

Update a column outside the filter and confirm the handler does not run, then update one inside it and confirm it does. Getting the filter too narrow is as common as having none, and it fails silently in the other direction.
The step no longer fires on changes to unrelated columns
The columns the handler actually reads are listed on the registration
backlog.performance.viewComplexity.given: The default view {componentName} on {tableName}, with {count} columns or linked entities
backlog.performance.viewComplexity.testR: Confirm nothing depends on the default view's column set: an export, a template or a script reading the grid. Trimming a default view is the kind of change that breaks something a fortnight later.
backlog.performance.viewComplexity.then: The table opens on a smaller default view and the wide view is still reachable
backlog.performance.viewComplexity.when: The default view has been trimmed and the wide version kept as a named alternative
backlog.quality.canvasDelegationWarnings: The canvas app {componentName}, with delegation warnings against {tableName}
Test against production volume, or a copy of it. Every one of these works in a development environment with two hundred rows, which is why the finding exists.
The app returns correct results against the full table, not only against the first five hundred rows
Each query over a table with real volume has been made delegable
backlog.quality.flowFailureRate.given: The flow {componentName}, failing {evidenceValue} of its runs
backlog.quality.flowFailureRate.testRequ: Reproduce the original failure before fixing anything. A flow fixed without reproducing the failure is a flow that will fail again on the same input.
backlog.quality.flowFailureRate.then: The failure rate over the following thirty days is below two percent, and any run that still fails does so for a reason somebody has written down
backlog.quality.flowFailureRate.when: The cause has been found and fixed
backlog.quality.flowNoErrorHandling.test: Force a failure in a non production environment and confirm the notification arrives. A configure run after setting that points at nothing looks identical to a working one in the designer.
backlog.quality.flowNoErrorHandling.then: The failure is reported to the agreed channel within one run, carrying the flow name, the run identifier and the failing action
backlog.quality.flowSize.testRequirement: Run the whole chain end to end with the same trigger data as the original and compare the outcome. Splitting a flow changes the failure boundaries, so a child that fails now leaves the parent in a state the original never had.
backlog.quality.flowSize.then: No resulting flow exceeds forty actions, and each one has a name saying what it does rather than what it is part of
backlog.quality.flowSize.when: It has been split into child flows along the steps a person would describe out loud
backlog.quality.formScriptOnLoadWeight.t: Measure form load before and after, and exercise each form. A library removed from a form where a handler still references it fails at the point the user clicks something, not at load.
Every form still behaves as it did, and the onload payload is smaller
backlog.quality.formScriptOnLoadWeight.w: Libraries are registered only on the forms that use them
backlog.quality.missingDescription.given: {count} custom {componentType} with no description in solution {solutionName}
backlog.quality.missingDescription.testR: Have somebody outside the team read ten of them and say what each component does. A description repeating the display name passes every automated check and helps nobody.
backlog.quality.missingDescription.then: Somebody who has never seen the solution can tell what each one does from its description alone
backlog.quality.missingDescription.when: A description has been written saying what the component is for and who asked for it
backlog.quality.namingInconsistent.testR: None on existing components. Renaming a schema name is not possible and renaming a display name breaks scripts, views and documentation that reference it, for a cosmetic gain.
backlog.quality.namingInconsistent.then: Components created after that date follow it
backlog.quality.namingInconsistent.when: A convention has been agreed and written where a new developer will find it
backlog.quality.pluginNoTracing.testRequ: Force an exception in a non production environment and read the trace log. Tracing that is written but never flushed, or written below the configured level, produces nothing and looks identical in the code.
backlog.quality.pluginNoTracing.then: A failure in production leaves a trace log entry naming the handler, the branch and the record
backlog.quality.pluginNoTracing.when: Tracing has been added at the entry and exit of each handler and at every branch that can throw
backlog.quality.pluginNotSandboxed.given: The plugin assembly {componentName}, registered outside sandbox isolation
backlog.quality.pluginNotSandboxed.testR: Import into a clean environment and exercise every registered step. Expect to find at least one thing that needed full trust, because that is usually why it was registered this way.
backlog.quality.pluginNotSandboxed.then: It imports into an online environment, and the behaviour that needed full trust either works within the sandbox or has been moved outside the platform
backlog.quality.pluginNotSandboxed.when: It has been rebuilt to run in sandbox isolation and registered in the database rather than on disk
The security role {componentName}, granting organisation level write on {tableName}
Have somebody who holds the role walk their actual daily tasks in a non production environment. Something will break, and finding out which thing in test is the entire purpose of this work item.
The people who hold the role can still do their work, and can no longer change records outside their scope
The privilege has been narrowed to business unit or user level
backlog.security.secretInDefinition.give: The {componentType} {componentName}, containing a credential in its definition
backlog.security.secretInDefinition.test: Rotate first and confirm the old value stops working. Moving the secret without rotating leaves a live credential in every copy of the solution file that has already been exported, and in source control history.
backlog.security.secretInDefinition.then: The exported solution contains no credential, and the component works with the new one
backlog.security.secretInDefinition.when: The credential has been rotated and the component reads it from Key Vault through an environment variable
